content: Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect condition in the `if` statement that checks the result of the `kill(pid, 0)` function. The original code used `if(!kill(pid, 0))`, which would incorrectly interpret a successful check (indicating the process is running) as a failure, leading to the `still_running` variable being set to false when it should not have been. The fix changes the condition to `if(kill(pid, 0))`, which correctly identifies when the process is not running, allowing the program to accurately determine the process's status.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect condition in the `if` statement that checks the result of the `kill(pid, 0)` function. The original code used `if(!kill(pid, 0))`, which would incorrectly interpret a successful check (indicating the process is running) as a failure, leading to the `still_running` variable being set to false when it should not have been. The fix changes the condition to `if(kill(pid, 0))`, which correctly identifies when the process is not running, allowing the program to accurately determine the process's status.
Patch:
From 3a061c367dc2654b9c3e14af62ce7adbd971fe7f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Brandon L Black <blblack@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Mar 2014 17:58:20 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] fix kill-status bug from 2ae7c831

---
 gdnsd/libgdnsd/libdmn/dmn.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/gdnsd/libgdnsd/libdmn/dmn.c b/gdnsd/libgdnsd/libdmn/dmn.c
index fe6b04f..7f8d654 100644
--- a/gdnsd/libgdnsd/libdmn/dmn.c
+++ b/gdnsd/libgdnsd/libdmn/dmn.c
@@ -366,7 +366,7 @@ static bool terminate_pid_and_wait(pid_t pid) {
             tv.tv_sec = 0;
             tv.tv_usec = 100000;
             select(0, NULL, NULL, NULL, &tv);
-            if(!kill(pid, 0)) {
+            if(kill(pid, 0)) {
                 still_running = false;
                 break;
             }
